title: Respan (YC W24)
summary: Open-source Rust AI gateway built around plugins

extra.author: Andydy25
extra.original_title: Launch HN: Respan (YC W24) – Open-source Rust AI gateway built around plugins

story_text.value:
Hey HN, this is Andy from Respan (https://www.respan.ai). We are building an open-source Rust AI gateway. It is a decoupled gateway, so everything is a plugin, including different providers, protocols (MCP, voice), modalities (images, videos), and gateway features (fallbacks, PII redaction, smart routing).

Instead of packaging tons of providers and features into one gateway, Respan provides a small core and public interfaces that teams can use to assemble the AI infrastructure their application needs. That way, users can build their own features as additional plugins without having to change the gateway's core.

Here’s a video demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pVv2ibXiTXM

There are countless LLM gateways and most of them solve a common problem: calling different providers from a single endpoint. However, adding new features can become prohibitively difficult. So developers can end up building another gateway to solve a specific problem.

We've been building our gateway based on LiteLLM since 2024, and now it's providing services for thousands of orgs. Each org needs different API key settings, routes, and limits. To support that, we kept wrapping LiteLLM, adding more features to it, and at one stage, our wrapper code exceeded 100,000 lines.

This January, a routine LiteLLM upgrade caused intermittent connection errors, and we had to roll back. We still haven't figured out the cause, but since then, we no longer upgrade LiteLLM directly and instead manually backport upstream fixes. These experiences made us realize that continuing to patch LiteLLM is not a sustainable long-term solution, and we had to redesign the gateway ourselves.

While redesigning our gateway, we wanted to make it easier to add features without breaking existing ones. Inspired by Nginx, we think an AI gateway should have a really small core, only responsible for dispatching events.

We believe that everything should be a plugin in our gateway, including providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini), protocols (chat, realtime voice, MCP), modalities (images, videos), and gateway features for reliability and security (smart routing, fallbacks, and PII redaction through example plugins). Beyond that, we want developers to be able to easily extend the gateway's capabilities by adding their own plugins, without touching the core. Adding a provider, even your own, is dead simple, because quirks are plugins too and there’s nothing magical about them. A provider is a short file, Mistral’s is 22 lines, and each quirk, like Groq putting token usage in its own field, gets its own test.

Respan Gateway does more than let you call Claude or Gemini models from the OpenAI SDK. It handles tools, images, and reasoning protocols automatically: an application based on the OpenAI Realtime API can also use Gemini Live through the gateway, though not every feature translates. A simple chat app can use MCP tools configured in the gateway, without implementing MCP itself.

We also parse requests into a shared structure. When the client and provider use the same API, we preserve provider-specific fields in their native format, even if our shared structure doesn't have a field for them. That way, the gateway can write them back instead of dropping them.

Here’s how it works:

An adapter hands each HTTP or WebSocket connection to the first client format that recognizes it. The format exposes the request as a two-way stream of typed input and output events. The core runs plugins in registration order, allowing them to choose a provider, filter or wrap either stream, make additional calls, return a response, or refuse the request. A provider format then opens the upstream connection.

If the client and provider use the same format and no plugin changes the payload, the original bytes and protocol-specific fields can pass through unchanged. When formats differ, they translate through shared types for messages, tool calls, results, streams, and usage. This stream model can represent both one-shot HTTP requests and long-lived bidirectional sessions.

The gateway is open source at https://github.com/respanai/respan-gateway under the MIT or Apache-2.0 license. You don't need to use Respan's hosted platform and can run it directly on your local machine. Build it from source, add your provider keys, and swap the base URL in a supported client. You can keep using the API your client already speaks. It's still pre-alpha.

We make money from our hosted platform (https://www.respan.ai/pricing), which runs the gateway for you with native observability and evals, along with unified billing.

If you’re building routing, tools, filtering, observability, or security for agents, we'd love to see it as a plugin. PLUGINS.md in the repo explains how to write one and links to the plugins we’ve created so far. Turning that into an ecosystem is basically our roadmap, and we welcome you to contribute your own plugins. We'd love to answer any questions and hear your feedback!

https://github.com/respanai/respan-gateway

title: Laminar (YC S24)
summary: RL-trained model that finds errors in agent traces

extra.author: skull8888888
extra.original_title: Launch HN: Laminar (YC S24) – RL-trained model that finds errors in agent traces

story_text.value:
Hi HN, we’re Robert and Din from Laminar (https://laminar.sh). We’ve been building open-source observability for AI agents since 2024. Recently, we released flow-1, a model trained with RL to find errors in agent traces. On our benchmark (https://laminar.sh/blog/flow-1), it matches GPT-6-sol in detection quality while being 23x cheaper. This makes it affordable to analyze every production agent trace, without sampling.

Here’s a one-minute walkthrough: https://youtu.be/KJa3h6ZJNLQ

We also put together a post with example traces and analyses from flow-1 and other models: https://laminar.sh/blog/flow-1-in-action

Agent observability is crowded, so instead of a bullet list of how Laminar differs from X, we’ll explain how we’re solving agent observability from first principles.

Agents now run for many steps and fail implicitly. An agent can click the wrong button or cite the wrong document while every call completes successfully. These errors are the most useful ones to catch and understand. To find them, you need to understand what the agent was trying to do and inspect its LLM calls and tool results. Simply looking at the final agent output is not enough.

Collecting traces alone doesn’t solve this. A lot of agent observability platforms are still data collectors at their core. You can end up paying to store traces that nobody has time to read or extract value from.

Using another LLM to inspect traces is THE solution, but capable models are expensive at scale and cheaper ones often miss errors or flag unrelated things.

So we built our model to solve exactly this problem. We finetuned a small OSS model and then post trained it with RL on thousands of synthetic investigations of realistic agent workflows in software, legal, customer support, etc. We got a model that is both good at agent trace analysis and very cheap to run.

flow-1 runs inside a harness we call Signals. It acts as a coding agent, treating an agent trace like a repo, with each span (an LLM call, tool call, etc.) as a file. It starts from a compressed string representation of a full agent trace and a user prompt, then greps across spans and reads the relevant ones in full.

The beauty of Signals is that it can respond to a general prompt. You can ask it to identify user frustration, check whether your browser agent completed a checkout, and so on. It’s not limited to raw error detection. It returns findings as JSON in a schema users can freely define. We call these signal events.

Once you’re analyzing every trace, you also have too many individual events to read. That’s why we automatically group similar signal events into clusters. You can see recurring problems and how often they happen, then drill into individual events and the traces behind them.

You can use traces from a cluster to build an eval dataset for that type of failure. You can then use your favourite coding agent to hillclimb on those evals and check that the fix works across these cases before shipping it to prod.

Trace → analyze → catch errors and form clusters → fix → release. Making this loop easy is why we built Laminar.

We’ve put the same thought into the rest of Laminar. Our blog (https://laminar.sh/blog) explains how looking closely at how agents actually work led us to build 20x trace compression, a custom SQL query engine and automatic task extraction.

Laminar is Apache 2.0 and self-hostable (https://github.com/lmnr-ai/lmnr). We make money from the managed cloud.

We’d love to hear how you track your agents’ performance today. How much do you learn from user feedback versus your own monitoring? And when you fix something, how do you check that it hasn’t introduced a different failure?

title: Maxwell
summary: A new kind of model that sits between code and hardware

extra.author: laginimaineb
extra.original_title: Maxwell: A new kind of model that sits between code and hardware

story_text.value:
Hi HN, I'm Gal from doubleAI. We've built Maxwell, a new kind of frontier model we call a Code Execution Model.

It sits between your code and the hardware. No humans in the loop! Maxwell makes the code run faster as it runs, without ever changing a single line.

Maxwell sees programs from the inside: traces, profiling information, and the data flowing through them. It adapts dynamically to the environment, including the hardware, what else is running, and what the inputs look like.

Code execution models change the way we approach coding. Today, Claude/Codex (and humans) keep re-optimising code for every different use-case hardware and data flow (think of LLM inference engines, like vLLM!). Our bet is that this is unnecessary, suboptimal, and that it does not scale. Instead, we think the right answer is to make code a living, thinking, thing.

Early access is open at heymaxwell.ai. Happy to answer questions here.

Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch
summary: Most large language models (LLMs) use transformer architectures with softmax attention. During inference, their key-value (KV) cache grows with the conversation or document context. This can reduce concurrency, increase serving cost, and force agentic applications to discard useful history. i14 designed Laplace 3B as a linear attention alternative. Its recurrent state stays at 29.5 MB per sequence, independent of context length. Working with AWS, i14 used native PyTorch support through TorchNeuron Native to bring this custom architecture to AWS Trainium2 . This preserved its Gated Linear Attention (GLA) design and Muon optimizer. On one trn2.48xlarge instance, Laplace 3B trained at about 120,000 tokens per second. The model served 11,544 output tokens per second across 1,280 concurrent sequences. This post explains the model design, the changes i14 made for Trainium2, and the training and inference results. About i14 i14 is an AI research and technology company that develops model architectures, components, and runtimes. Its work draws on AI, computational cognitive science, and research into how biological systems learn over time. i14 applies these ideas to models that can retain long-range context without allowing serving state to grow with every token. title: Work management context for AI agents with Smartsheet MCP on AWS
summary: AI agents are most useful when they can act on the real work happening across your organization. Work management involves complex, cross-functional tasks such as updating project timelines, reassigning tasks, and surfacing status. AI agents can support you with these without anyone switching tools. Smartsheet , the work management platform for managing projects, portfolios, and operations, has launched a generally available Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server. With the Smartsheet MCP Server , AI assistants can read, write, and manage Smartsheet data through a standardized protocol. The protocol spans more than 40 tools for exploring, creating, and managing sheets, rows, columns, and automations. You can update task statuses, create rows, and modify project structure directly through natural language. In this post, we walk through two ways you can connect it to your existing workflows. Amazon Quick is an agentic AI workspace built for business users, project managers, and operations teams. They can ask questions, update sheets, and build dashboards through natural language without writing code. Kiro is an agentic IDE where developers connect to Smartsheet through MCP to reference project specs, update task status, and track dependencies without leaving their coding workflow. title: From data to decisions: Conversational supply chain intelligence with Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
summary: Giving supply chain teams direct access to the systems behind their decisions. Every supply chain generates constant signals: orders in approval, shifting lead times, slowing ports, drifting prices, disruptions. The problem isn’t scarce data. It’s the distance between the data and the decision-maker. Answering “which top-revenue SKUs are exposed to the current port closure, and what will it cost?” used to mean knowing which system held each piece and stitching them together by hand while the domain expert waited. Could that manager instead ask in plain language and get an actionable, cross-system answer in seconds? Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is the intelligence layer, exposing enterprise Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers as a composable tool layer. Amazon Quick turns that into action for personas with no setup. Answers come from live systems of record and grounded documents, not model recall, and every change waits for a named human. In this post, we walk through this pattern end to end, from a conversational walkthrough in Amazon Quick to the AgentCore tool layer behind it, and we show you how to deploy it yourself. summary: GPT-OSS-20B is an open-weight reasoning model that thinks in English. Ask it to reason in French, German, Spanish, or Italian and it acknowledges the instruction, then produces its chain-of-thought in English anyway. On a 50-example multilingual reasoning test, the base model reasoned in the correct target language only 22 percent of the time. That 22 percent was almost entirely the English examples (English 100 percent, French 0 percent, German 10 percent, Spanish 0 percent, Italian 0 percent). For teams deploying reasoning models for non-English users, that gap matters. A user who asks a question in French expects the model to reason and answer in French, not to switch to English mid-thought. Closing that gap is a fine-tuning problem. It raises a question every team faces once they start customizing open-weight models: supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), or both? In this post, we walk through how we fine-tuned GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod . We show when SFT alone was sufficient and when GRPO added measurable value on top. title: Securing AI agent identity with X.509 PKI on AWS
summary: When AI agents access databases, APIs, and sensitive business operations, establishing cryptographic identity through X.509 public key infrastructure (PKI) becomes a critical requirement. The core challenge is proving which agent made a request, preventing forgery between agents, and confirming that each agent acts only on behalf of an authorized user. Traditional approaches such as sharing API keys between components or passing OAuth tokens through agent chains fall short of the zero-trust requirements that enterprise deployments demand. Multi-agent AI frameworks increasingly use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to connect agents to external tools and data sources. MCP defines how a large language model (LLM)-powered agent invokes tools such as database queries or email operations. However, MCP has no built-in authentication standard. It is transport-agnostic by design. This creates a critical gap: Without proper identity mechanisms, any component could impersonate an agent, replay intercepted credentials, or invoke tools without authorization. In this post, we show you how to address this gap using Keyfactor EJBCA combined with AWS services. title: Push-based KV transfer to improve TTFT and TPOT for disaggregated inference in vLLM
summary: vLLM is an open-source inference and serving engine for large language models (LLMs). LLM inference has two distinct phases: prefill, which processes the input prompt and builds the key-value (KV) cache, and decode, which uses that cache to generate output one token at a time. These phases have different compute, memory, and scaling characteristics. Prefill-decode (P-D) disaggregation runs them on separate engine instances, allowing each phase to scale and be optimized independently. This can improve resource utilization, throughput, and latency under load. However, it also requires transferring the KV cache from the prefill instance to the decode instance before token generation can begin, making efficient KV transfer critical to time-to-first-token (TTFT). One of the ways vLLM performs this transfer is through the NVIDIA Inference Xfer Library (NIXL) connector , which moves KV blocks over interconnects that support Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA), such as AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter ( AWS EFA , the low-latency RDMA network used across servers in AWS). On supported instance types , AWS EFA supports GPUDirect RDMA and Neuron Direct RDMA. title: Improve TTFT for multi-turn agentic workloads with bi-directional KV transfer in vLLM
summary: Multi-turn agentic workloads build on accumulated context as an agent reasons, invokes tools, and incorporates earlier results. With each new turn, the client resends the conversation history, including system instructions, prior prompts, tool results, and model responses, causing the growing context to be processed repeatedly. In Prefill-decode (P-D) disaggregation , each request is split across specialized nodes: the prefill node processes the prompt and builds its key-value (KV) cache, then the decode node retrieves those KV blocks and generates the response. Conventional disaggregated serving, however, only transfers KV cache in one direction: from prefill to decode node. This one-directional flow creates two inefficiencies for multi-turn workloads. First, after generating a response, the decode node holds KV cache entries for both the prompt and the newly generated tokens. When processing the next turn, the prefill node cannot retrieve those entries, so it must recompute the KV projections for the previous response tokens. Second, the decode node maintains the session state while the prefill nodes don’t, increasing the probability of cache eviction for active sessions on the prefill nodes. 而宁德时代正在通过技术合作、股权投资等方式扩大换电业务规模。赛豆科技旗下 AIVA 品牌首款量产车 AIVA ME7 将采用换电模式，宁德时代提供电池技术及充换电体系支持，具体方案还在规划中。（来源：晚点 Auto、财联社） 曝高通将启动全球裁员 据路透社报道，高通 CEO 克里斯蒂亚诺·安蒙近期在一份内部备忘录中告知员工，公司将在年度员工评估后，开展以绩效为重点的全球裁员，相关通知将于 11 月开始发出。 安蒙表示，此举旨在建立更强的绩效文化，并解决公司持续未能达到预期的情况。备忘录未披露裁员人数，路透社也暂时无法确定此次裁员的规模。 路透社在报道中指出作为全球最大的智能手机芯片制造商之一，高通今年受到消费电子产品销售低迷的冲击，存储芯片价格飙升抑制了关键市场的需求。 随着业务向快速增长的 AI 数据中心市场拓展，高通预计，2027 财年，公司芯片销售收入的大部分将来自智能手机以外的业务。（来源：凤凰网科技） C919 大飞机国产发动机将进入取证试飞阶段 日前，网友爆料称，运 20 飞行台上挂载了国产自研大飞机 C919 的国产替代发动机 CJ1000A 开始试飞了，推测应该该发动机进入了取证试飞阶段。 航发科技公司上周在互动平台上回应过 CJ1000A 的进展，表示公司承制的 CJ 1000A 发动机相关零部件设计构型及工艺路线已实现初步冻结，后续不排除根据 TC Only 批次制造符合性检查开展情况、总师单位取证试验结果发生局部调整优化的可能。 CJ1000A 发动机的目标是实现 C919 现有发动机 LEAP-1C 的替代，这就意味着需要在动力、经济、维护等方面看齐 LEAP-1C。 报道表示：考虑到 LEAP-1C 是当前最先进的商用发动机之一，CJ1000A 的难度可想而知，所以这也是这款发动机打磨了 10 多年的原因，需要每个环节都要做到可靠稳定。明年能拿证就很乐观了，正式运营可能还要等到 28-29 年。（来源：快科技） 杨立昆吐槽特斯拉飞行汽车不实用，马斯克回怼：「放屁」 人工智能先驱人物、AMI Labs 创始人兼董事长杨立昆（Yann LeCun）最近在 X 平台点评了特斯拉刚刚发布的「飞行汽车」Roadster，认为这款产品「完全不实用」。 杨立昆表示，这辆汽车用的只是压缩空气，比冲很差（不到 50 秒）。即使假设压缩空气占整车质量的 50%，在推重比大于 1.0 的情况下，有效推力也只能维持不到 10 秒，实际上可能只有 5 秒左右。 因此他表示，这辆车肯定只是一个空心的轻量化外壳，加上大型压缩空气罐。发布会很有意思，但产品完全不实用。 马斯克对此回应称：「我冲着你的方向放了个屁。」 而杨立昆则回怼道：「如果腹部压力足够大，放屁确实可能让你飞起来。仔细想想，你的汽车也是靠同样原理驱动的：一个压力高达 700 bar、容量 600 升、持续 3 秒、声音巨大的屁。【希望里面没有甲烷，和那些臭得要死的化合物】。」（来源：IT之家） 《GTA 6》数字版预购突破 600 万份，销售额接近 6 亿美元 距离正式发售仍有一个多月时间，Rockstar Games 备受期待的开放世界大作《侠盗猎车手 6》（GTA 6）已经展现出惊人的市场号召力。 根据市场分析机构 Sensor Tower 最新估算，截至 10 月 13 日，该游戏全球数字版预购量已突破 600 万份，预计带来约 5.94 亿美元收入，成为近年来游戏行业最受瞩目的预售产品之一。 报告还显示，高价版本成为玩家购买主力。售价 100 美元的 Ultimate Edition 终极版占据绝大多数预购份额。即便单独统计这一高端版本，其销售曲线依然远高于近年来任何同类游戏产品。（来源：cnBeta） 理想宣布电池保障计划：电池不自燃、碰撞不起火终身保障 10 月 20 日，在理想汽车 Power Day 电动技术发布会上，理想正式发布完整自研三电技术体系「连山」。 同时，理想推出「连山电池保障计划」，提供双重终身保障：一是「电池不自燃终身保障」，因原厂电池质量问题导致自燃且车辆达到报废条件，补偿同等配置新车；二是「碰撞不起火终身保障」，因碰撞或底盘剐蹭导致起火且达到报废条件，补偿车损险保单额与保险实际赔付金额差额。（来源：凤凰网科技） 马斯克股权薪酬曝光，为员工中位数 250 万倍 据福布斯报道，特斯拉当地时间周一向美国证券交易委员会（SEC）提交的 14A title: 设计师的第一个 Personal Agent，可能就是 Lovart 2.0 的 Arti 了
summary: 2025 年，Lovart 作为全球首款设计 Agent 开始出现在各大设计师社区。第一次用 AI 能力把整个设计流程串联起来。从最初的设计思路、到最终图片或视频的设计物料，终于被完整的放到一块画布上完成。 随着在生成能力和指令遵循程度上的进步，AI 越发能够满足人们现实世界的真实需求，muse 此时带起关于 personal agent 的讨论显得恰逢其时。AI 在能力上已经具备了可观的解决问题的能力，下一步就是如何个性化的解决「我」的问题，以及更主动的解决问题。 放到设计里，Personal Agent 带来了一些新的想象力。比如一套物料做完，下一个项目还会来。设计师喜欢什么配色、哪些版式已被否过，总不能每次开工都重新交代，那它能否持续性的理解设计师的风格变化？又或者设计前期调研、每周做一批物料这些日常的重复性工作，能不能也交代一次，让 AI 往后按时做？ 这些事决定了，眼下 AI 能把设计这件事推动到什么地步。 设计体系里，到现在用过 Lovart 的专业创作者已经达到数千万，它或许是当下最适合回答这个问题的，在迭代到 Lovart 2.0 后，它拿出了全球首个个人设计 agent——Arti。 01 Arti，个人设计 Agent Arti 不只是一个工具，而是一个真正接住完整设计工作的个人设计 Agent。 你交给它一个完整的设计需求，它不只负责生成，还会主动去调研、找参考。甚至它会查看画布检查信息有没有遗漏、排版有哪些地方需要调整，并根据你的反馈继续修改。这当中反复出现的工作也会被整理成 Skill，下次再遇到相似的需求，它就能沿用这些做法，省下重新交代和重复操作的工夫。 但在这之前，Arti 在设计领域首先要迈过的门槛，是对于设计师的个人风格和设计 taste 的理解。这也是为什么 Arti 是从 「 记忆 」 功能诞生的。 进入 Arti 的第一件事，是告诉 Agent 你是谁。 你需要先告诉 Arti 你从事的领域，比如电商、营销、内容创作或者其他的行业，然后就会进入下一步更细致的询问页面——我第一次体验 Arti 的时候正好有一位在日化消费品牌做过设计师的朋友坐在旁边，所以我借着他的人设，选择的是电商。 Arti 会问的非常细节，除了主要做的设计物料种类，还会询问我作为设计师的身份，是甲方、乙方或者接单的独立设计师。对应不同场景下，Arti 和设计师有着不同的协同方式，这些它都考虑进去了。 确定了协同方式之后，之后是确定审美偏好这一步。 先选择一种默认的审美偏向是意料之中的，但让人意外的是 Arti 有一个问题是「哪些情况不按默认风格来？」。坐在我旁边做过电商公司设计师的朋友看到了眼泪要喷出来了——「平台强制规范、合作限定...... 这个 Arti 知道我们设计师的苦。」 一系列问询题目的答案结合后会成为设计师个性化 Arti 的起点，但这些肯定不足以说明一位设计师的 taste，所以在页面最下方的「常用资产」一栏，你可以直接把自己以前的设计稿、文档或者海报放进去，更直接的让 Arti 来理解你的风格和偏好。 当然，除了提供你在 Arti 之外的设计素材，你也可以把之前在 Arti 或者 Lovart 上做的设计放进去成为未来的参考。Arti 是一个极具成长性的 Agent，记忆是成长的原点，你每一次在 Arti 中发生的成功或失败的创作，都会推动你的 Arti 持续进化。 02 最怕懂我的人还主动 和所有设计类的 Agent 不同的是，Arti 更像是一个有完整设计领域经验的 Personal AI。Personal AI 的概念是一套新的技术栈的封装组合出的新的产品形态，而 Arti 更像是把这个新的产品形态里一些最重要的特质做了单独强化——比如对于主动性的重视。 这意味着它会更主动的参与整个设计流程前、中、后期。那些设计工作流里最痛苦的事，最渴望甩给一个经验点满的高精力同事分担的工作，现在 Arti 可以一个不落的都主动接过去。 设计方法的前期工作里，最巨大的工作量，毫无疑问是调研和找那些参考。 拿到一个新的设计项目时，也同时会拿到需求方的更多背景要求和表达偏好，这意味着在它落到最终确定的设计方案之前，有许多关于背景资料调研、风格参考的案头工作。 拿我身边这位消费品公司的设计师亲身经历举个例子。他在画电商大促的第一张海报前，得先弄清卖给谁、主推什么、优惠怎么讲，再翻竞品店铺和往期活动，比较主视觉、商品摆放、价格与赠品的呈现方式。 随后在花瓣、Pinterest 等平台反复换关键词，找配色、字体、构图、光影和场景参考，下载、归类、拆解，拼成情绪板。每张参考还得判断：是否符合品牌，能否突出卖点，放不放得下促销文案，能不能延展到首页、横幅和商品主图。甚至看中的配色、构图和材质，可能分散在不同案例里，组合起来又未必协调。 现在 Arti 会主动把这个活儿接过来。你可以在项目对话框中直接唤起 Arti，让它以当前对话中你给出的调研背景和参考素材来做全面调研。 举个例子，我现在想做一个攀岩品牌的电商大促的物料设计方案，我给了它一些设计语言的关键词和一些参考图片，它给了我几个可行的大方向，我选择了其中一个方案然后叫 Arti 帮我调研一下这个方案更多细节的考量。 Arti 的调研还挺细致，从主 KV 的几个核心意象的大小比例、色调的选择以及文字信息的设计几个方面都做了分析，并且让我很意外的是它主动找到了一个攀岩品牌 Black Diamond 的品牌海报来做了参考。 这份调研报告可以直接被转进项目对话里（你也可以继续优化或者提出更多的调研需求），进一步充实这个设计方案的背景往下推进。 调研是设计前期的部分，更大的工作量是在真正进入设计流程后。 设计师们期待 AI 能够让设计物料这件事走上福特生产线，但一旦碰到复杂的设计场景，或者要围绕一个确定的设计语言出多种物料设计，AI 在长对话、多轮修改中就会暴露出对上下文理解的不遵循，问题落到生产出的物料上就是风格的严重不统一。 这是设计师在使用 AI 时最大的卡点之一，而 Arti 会在整个画布层面上来自动检查风格一致性与规范。 上面这个攀岩的设计方案往下推进后，我让 Arti 试着出几个适合电商平台 banner 风格的设计海报，之后把设计海报先收敛在电商首页 banner 位的时候，Arti 发现其中有一张海报不是电商首页 banner 的 3:1 比例。它在对话中发现了这一点，并且提示可以一键调整尺寸。 没有一击即中的设计，在最终定稿之前，每一版的设计物料都会有需求方或者自己团队来的修改意见。一个好的设计 Agent 当然也要了解这一点。所以 Arti 把多轮的反馈改稿这件事也自动化了。 Arti 最适合的打开方式，或许是把它理解成一个能够多方协同的在线设计 Agent。Arti 支持他人在画布上评论修改意见，然后它可以自动的汇总，进一步理解这些修改意见并且提出具体的优化方案，之后我要做的，只是把这个方案放回项目的对话框，然后执行这些改进动作即可。 而设计师在画布上的每一次设计操作，都会在 Arit 的进化日志中被记录下来。当它察觉到你在反复在执行一些相似的设计流程，比如服装上新时模特上身的参考图，或者电子产品上新时的多角度特写，Arti 可以从你的操作和产出中总结出确定的设计思路，自动沉淀为可复用的 Skill。 以服装、鞋类产品的模特上身图举个例子，在我反复做过几次后，这一整套设计流程就会在 Arti 个人主页的「我学会的」里出现。再有类似的设计需求，只需要把新的产品图放入参考背景，然后直接唤起这套流程即可。当然，你可以在」管理技能」中继续优化这一套流程，以及微调一些需要改动的环节。 带着做一遍，然后同类型的活儿都可以交给它——这简直是每个设计师梦想中的完美实习生。但这可能是实习生的极限，不是 Arit 的极限。 03 一个能够自驱动的设计助手 做设计的朋友一直在我电脑旁边看着我演示。我问他，要是不设条件，你最想要一个什么样的设计 Agent ? 「一个能力和审美完全复刻我，但又不厌倦上班，啥事不往心里去，有无限精力和创作激情的，直接帮我把所有活儿干了的助手。」 养熟了之后，完全让他自己干活——这其实要比刚才提到的 Arti 已经体现出的每项单独能力都更复杂。但这件事 Arti 也已经在做了，叫「设计委托」。 创建一个设计委托，输入具体的设计指令和参考素材，设定好执行时间和频率，就可以让 Arit 来自主推进设计方案，无论是批量生成、重复处理还是多任务工作，都可以经过一次委托，省去反复操作和等待的时间。 我试了试把刚才攀岩的海报设计需求放入设计委托，新的海报设计会准时在拟定的时间点出现在个人项目页上。 委托的执行当然也会消耗积分，所以在一开始新建委托时你需要设定好积分消耗上限。而根据使用者对这个设计委托在各个层面的考量，你可以灵活的选择是用「快速」、「均衡」或者更强的「专家」模式来执行你的委托。这意味着或许一整个设计团队，都可以合理的通过 Arti 的设计委托来提效。 「专家」模式可以在图片和视频生成上达到 4k 的水准，并且具备复杂规划的能力，创意团队可以应付那些非常精细的核心设计物料；运营团队需要结合不同场景的产品图来大批量的铺设，或者需要围绕一个 IP 形象大批量的出图，则可以通过在质量和速度之间更加平衡的「均衡」模式来执行；而营销环节中那些图片和视频之外的文案灵感收集和创作，「快速」模式就可以应付了。 拿最近的双 11 举个例子，比如双 11 主视觉定稿了。接下来的需求是：42 个 SKU，每个要出淘宝主图、详情页头图、小红书封面、朋友圈海报四个尺寸，一共 168 张图。你可以把它拆成一个更明确的设计委托： 按项目里已确认的双 11 主视觉风格（上传主视觉），为附件表格中的 42 个

title: 1 分钟售罄、发货排到明年，iPhone Duo 卖爆背后的真相
summary: 人们已经很多年没见过，苹果的新品被这样抢了。 10 月 16 日晚 8 点，苹果首款折叠屏 iPhone Duo 开启预购。社交媒体上流传的说法是， 开售 1 分钟，全型号库存就空了，京东、天猫页面相继显示售罄 。 大约 40 分钟后， 苹果官网的预计送达时间已经跳到了 2027 年 1 月底 。 几个小时后，大洋彼岸的美国东部时间上午 8 点，同样的剧情再演一遍。分析师 Max Weinbach 在 X 上说，纽约及周边、康涅狄格州的门店大约 3 分钟就被抢光。半小时内，美国所有配置的交付日期都变成了 1 月 25 日。eBay 上，一台 2TB 版的预购机挂出了 5000 美元的成交价，比官方价格高出 1800 美元。 这不是中国市场独有的狂热，而是一场苹果新品全球同步的抢购。 iPhone Duo 卖爆的背后，真的是产品太牛，创新性十足，还是产能不足逼出的热卖？ 「秒罄」这两个字，其实藏着两个完全不同的故事。一个关于需求，一个关于产能。 01 太整齐的交付日期 先看一个容易被忽略的细节。 iPhone Duo 这次在美国、中国、英国、德国、日本、印度等约 70 个国家和地区同步开启预购 。开售之后，美国和英国最早的交付日期都是 1 月 25 日，国行显示的是 1 月底。 市场规模、消费习惯、竞争格局完全不同的几个国家，交付日期却几乎对齐。 这更像是苹果在全球范围内按配额统一分货的结果，而不是各地需求恰好一样旺。 换句话说，首批能放出来的货就那么多，分到每个市场的量都不大，哪里都是几分钟被抢完。 这一点从黄牛市场也能看出来。 国内顶配机型的加价被报到 7000 元以上，甚至有说法称破万 ；美国 1TB 和 2TB 两个版本的转售价都比官方价格高出约 1800 美元。以 2TB 版来算，美国的溢价幅度大约是五成多，和国内的情况相差无几。 两边的「热度」高度相似，恰恰说明真正决定热度上限的，是供给。 02 让人遗憾的产能 如果把时间拨回到一个多月前，iPhone Duo 的产能问题其实早有端倪。 日经亚洲 8 月底的报道称， 苹果当时每天只能生产「几百台」iPhone Duo ，远远低于一款常规 iPhone 新品的爬坡节奏。9 月中旬，界面新闻援引供应链消息称，富士康的组装良率只比 60% 高一点，要提升到成熟水平，可能还需要半年到一年。 问题的核心，在那枚特殊设计的铰链上。 供应链消息显示，iPhone Duo 的铰链由 100 多个零件组成，外盖还用到了 3D 打印工艺。原本的主力供应商安费诺产能没能达到苹果的预期，苹果随后加大了台湾新日兴的供货比例。屏幕这一侧也不轻松，三星显示的折叠 OLED 面板良率同样偏低，部分原因是苹果在最后阶段改了设计。 分析师 Jeff Pu 因此把 iPhone Duo 今年的出货预测从 700 万台下调到 600 万台。他给出的理由很直接，是铰链拖了后腿，而不是需求不足。 需要说明的是，60% 良率不等于卖出去的手机有四成是坏的，它意味着有相当比例的机器第一次组装没有通过苹果的品控，需要返工或报废，生产因此变得又慢又贵。 说白了，苹果选择了「宁可少卖，也不能卖坏」。对第一代折叠屏来说，这几乎是唯一正确的选择。 当然，这些消息大多来自匿名的供应链渠道，苹果并没有正式确认过。 03 想买的人，也是真的多 如果只是货少，iPhone Duo 的故事不会这么好看。 开售前，仅京东一个平台的预约人数就被报道突破 200 万，也有说法称超过 300 万。不管哪个数字更准确，都远远高于首批的货量。 更值得玩味的是价格。 iPhone Duo 国行 256GB 版起售价 15999 元，2TB 顶配是 26499 元；美版起售价 1999 美元，顶配 3199 美元，这是苹果历史上最贵的一部手机。 在一个连「贵」都不足以形容的价位上还能秒罄，抢的已经不只是一部折叠屏，而是苹果的品牌溢价。 还有一层原因是「等待」。 折叠屏这个品类已经卖了七年，三星、华为、荣耀、OPPO、vivo 轮番迭代，苹果却一直按兵不动。 这些年里，攒下了一大批「等苹果做了再说」的用户 。他们未必是折叠屏的忠实拥趸，但他们相信苹果会是那个把折叠屏「做对」的人。 资本市场显然也愿意相信这一点。Deepwater 的 Gene Munster 认为 iPhone Duo 首年出货可能接近 2000 万台，Bloomberg Intelligence 也表示销量将超过他们此前 1400 万台的预测。 不过 Counterpoint 和 TrendForce 给出的今年预测都在 500 万到 600 万台之间，几家机构的分歧之大，本身就说明了一件事。 苹果没有公布首批到底放出了多少货，所以「秒罄」能证明有人想买，却证明不了苹果能卖出多少台。 04 卖爆背后的不同故事 把中国和美国放在一起看，会发现同一场抢购背后，是两个完全不同的市场。 在美国，折叠屏是三星的地盘。三星自己的数据显示，Galaxy Z Fold 8 系列在美国的销量比上一代高出约 30%。对美国用户来说，iPhone Duo 更像是苹果给折叠屏这个品类「正名」，把一个小众品类推向大众。 在中国，故事要复杂得多。 国内折叠屏的主角是华为。Omdia 的数据显示，今年上半年全球书本式折叠屏市场，华为拿下了 57% 的份额。但整个中国折叠屏市场的日子并不好过，已经连续三个季度同比下滑，IDC 预计全年还会下降 26.7%，原因之一正是苹果折叠屏在中国的供货有限，很多人在观望。 这意味着，苹果在中国点燃的，是一个原本正在降温的品类。 更大的背景是，苹果在中国的整体表现其实比很多人想象中要好。今年三季度中国手机市场整体下滑 15.4%，苹果出货只下降了 4.3%，份额反而提升到 17.8%，仅次于华为的

title: DeepSeek 新模型登顶开源模型榜首；国内 55% 算力用于视频和短剧？豆包发言人辟谣；微信发起公众号小说改编微短剧激励｜极客早知道
summary: DeepSeek 新模型登顶 Code Arena WebDev 开源模型榜首 10 月 19 日，AI 模型评测平台 Arena 宣布，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017（Max）超过 Kimi K3（Max），成为 Code Arena: WebDev 榜单排名最高的开源模型。 截至目前，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 在该榜单上得分为 1670 分，超过了Kimi K3（Max）、Mimo-V2.6 Flash等开源模型，也超过了Muse Spark 1.3（Max）、Claude Opus 5（High）、Grok 4.7（xHigh）等闭源模型，仅落后 GPT-6 Sol（Max）12 分。 该模型于 10 月 17 日推出，在软件工程能力 DeepSWE v1.1 测试中，其得分超GPT-6 Astra、GPT-6.1 Sol、Claude Opus 5等模型，单项任务平均费用较上一版本下降约六成。DeepSeek 称其模型支持「许愿式编程」，可一键生成游戏、3D 建模等。网友实测该模型生成速度比 GPT-6.1 超快模式还要快。 价格方面，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 在高峰时段的每百万 Token 输入（缓存未命中）价格为 2 元，输出价格为 8 元；空闲时段的输入（缓存未命中）价格为 1 元，输出价格为 4 元。若输入缓存命中，每百万 Token 输入价格在高峰时段为 0.04 元，空闲时段为 0.02 元，综合成本约为 Kimi K3 的 1/10。 Arena 发布的对比图显示，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 进入了 Code Arena 的「帕累托前沿」，即图中的绿色折线，这说明目前没有其他模型能同时做到比它更便宜、且得分更高。 （来源：新智元） 特斯拉声明没有速成车，陶琳称安全稳定可靠、让人安心是最大的豪华 10 月 19 日消息，特斯拉官方发微博，称特斯拉没有「速成车」。特斯拉官方表示，特斯拉拥有完整的直营体系（覆盖买车、提车、用车、修车、换车），没有 4S 店，销售、交付、客服、技师全是自家人，大品牌 + 完整的直营体系正是消费者放心买、安心用的最大底气。 特斯拉公司副总裁陶琳随后转发该博文并表示，「安全稳定可靠，让人安心是最大的豪华。」 特斯拉此前宣布，2026 年第三季度，特斯拉全球生产了超 46.4 万辆电动车，交付了超 48.6 万辆（同比下降 2%）；储能产品装机量达 13.7 吉瓦时。（来源：IT 之家） iPhone 18 Pro 系列国内销量超 408 万，开售三周破 400 万 10 月 19 日，博主 @RD 观测 公布苹果旗舰手机最新销量数据。截至 2026 年第 41 周，也就是 10 月 5 日至 10 月 11 日，iPhone 18 Pro 系列国内累计激活销量（Sell out）约为 408.09 万台。CNMO 科技注意到，该系列于 9 月 18 日正式开售，上市约三周时间累计销量已经突破 400 万台。 这也是 iPhone 18 Pro 系列上市以来销量继续快速增长的最新数据。Counterpoint Research 此前公布的数据也显示，iPhone 18 Pro 系列上市首周在中国市场的销量同比增长 12%，并帮助苹果在第 38 周登上中国智能手机周销量榜首。当时 iPhone 18 Pro 系列仅在该统计周内销售 3 天，因此新品带来的短期拉动较为明显。（来源：手机中国） Claude Code 九成代码由 AI 自写自审，仅高风险场景需人工 10 月 19 日，Anthropic 团队披露 Claude Code 约 90% 的代码由自身生成，大部分代码审核工作也由 AI 完成，2025 年 6 月到 9 月其合并 PR 量翻倍，回滚率反而下降超四成。 团队摒弃人工逐行审核的传统思路，以回滚率、事故率为核心指标，搭建起七层代码检查体系，通过多 AI Agent 分头排查 Bug、投票筛选意见，再按改动风险等级匹配不同强度的人工审批，依托类似瑞士奶酪模型的多层校验机制防控风险。（来源：新智元） 马斯克：Optimus 人形机器人和 Cybercab 将构成特斯拉绝大部分价值 10 月 19 日，特斯拉公司首席执行官埃隆·马斯克于周日在 X 平台发文称，公司的 Optimus 人形机器人与 Cybercab 自动驾驶汽车，将构成特斯拉价值的「绝大部分」，重申他将重心放在机器人与人工智能领域。

title: AI 里没有答案的问题，需要一场「深谈」
summary: 去年，极客公园创新大会第一次办起「小场深谈」。场子都不大，百人左右围坐在一起。 有些瞬间仍然记忆犹新。 在「超级个体」专场，一位观众站起来。他刚从大厂跳槽到一家小厂，正用 AI 做自己的第一款产品。他向嘉宾说出自己的困惑：我还在打工，做公众号、视频号，早晚会被老板和同事刷到。这个冲突，怎么解？ 在「硬控 AI」专场，有人直接向刚刚离职的小米 AI 眼镜负责人提问：如果给你两个亿，你会去做哪种 AI 眼镜？有人继续追问，你觉得豆包手机助手到底是真需求还是伪需求？ 在「重塑关系」专场，一位精神科医生，问做陪伴机器人的嘉宾：你是希望它把人带回现实社会的交往，还是给这个家添一个新成员？ 这些问题都不「大」，但都很真，带着一个人具体的处境，来自坐在你旁边的人。 有老朋友说，这让他们想起极客公园 17 年前的样子——在借来的索尼探梦地下室里，一群人席地而坐。 如果你参加过去年的「小场深谈」，很可能还记得这种 Vibe。不是发布会式的提问，更像小场子里几个人围坐时，把一个人正在卡住、关心的事摊开来聊。 去年的「小场深谈」，共设置了 4 个主题专场，包涵 12 场深度访谈，数百位观众走进小场，165 个朋友甚至同时买了主舞台和「小场」的票：既听了主会场的趋势判断，也不舍得错过小场里「深谈」的收获。还有超过不少人专程为某一场深谈而来。 大会后的购票调研里，超过六成观众把「话题兴趣」排在首位，为了聊自己真正关心的问题而来。 这让我们确认： 在信息过载的时代，有些问题，听 AI 解释一百遍，不如和「最有料的人」当面聊一次。嘉宾谈得尽兴，观众提出高质量的问题，一场访谈变成真正的共同创作。 IF 2026「小场深谈」现场部分精彩瞬间 今年 12 月 5 日、6 日，极客公园创新大会 2027 将在北京举行，主题是「Revaluation 价值，另有答案」。 AI 冲击下，价值的标准正在被重新评估。哪些旧经验值得重新审视，哪些新机会正在出现？ 最迫切的那些议题，网络上、AI 里都没有现成答案。 因此，在主舞台之外，我们将继续保留「小场深谈」——一个更小、更近、更主动的交流空间： 更深： 围绕一个方向，几小时的深度访谈与探讨，把一个问题聊透； 更近： 实干派嘉宾与观众面对面，传递最坦诚的思考； 更主动： 你不只是听众，可以提问，成为这场讨论的共同创作者。 值得聊的话题也在跟着变。 目前，小场的具体主题与最终场次仍在筹备中，但一批 候选话题方向 已经摆上桌面。与其关起门来做决定，不如把选择权交给极客公园的朋友们： 具身智能： 机器人从演示走向落地，真正卡在哪里？让一线团队聊聊那些「只有做过才知道」的阻力与加速度。 硬件创新： AI 时代，一个好产品的定义和实现路径正在被如何重写？好硬件的「新图纸」和「新供应链」应该是怎样的？ Personal AI： 从「提醒你」到「替你办」。当 AI 开始持续替一个人做事，它能替你做到哪一步？我们又该如何与它相处？ AI 娱乐： 当生成变得容易，「值得」由什么决定？产能爆发之后，什么内容值得被看见、值得付费，新的娱乐形式能否成立？ AI 落地： 模型不会自己走进现场。从「调用多少 Token」到「创造多大价值」，真正做出结果的企业，跨过了哪些障碍？ Maker 与新匠人： 当 3D 打印、CNC 等工具走进个人工作台，想法变成实物的路径正在变短。一个人的兴趣，能有多大的想象空间？ …… 投出你想聊的话题 你的 投票 ，会直接影响今年哪些话题被优先推进、请谁来聊、聊到什么深度。 我们希望带着你的选择，去邀请 真正有料 的人，聊出你想听的答案。 现在，在 文末投票 中选出你最想聊的话题方向（可多选），也欢迎在 评论区 补充你想聊、却还没被列出的问题。 今年 12 月，在北京，我们面对面，围坐在一起，把 AI 时代最值得聊的真问题，聊得更清楚。 特别预告 老朋友们都知道，极客公园创新大会的门票，几乎每年都会在会前提前售罄。去年即便临时加票，依然让不少关注 IF 的朋友抱憾未能来到现场。 如果你依然相信极客公园对科技脉搏的敏锐觉察，如果你也想在岁末年终，为自己寻找一份面向未来的确定性与安定感： IF 2027 官方门票将于 11 月初开售，请及时留意「极客公园」公众号，或有限量早鸟优惠票掉落哦～提早锁定，真正踏实。 请在手机微信登录投票 你最想聊的话题方向是什么?（多选） 具身智能：机器人从演示走向落地,真正卡在哪里？让一线团队聊聊那些「只有做过才知道」的阻力与加速度。 硬件创新：Al时代，一个好产品的定义和实现路径正在被如何重写好硬件的「新图纸」和「新供应 链」应该是怎样的？ Personal AI：从「提醒你」到「替你办」。当Al开始持续替一个人做事，它能替你做到哪一步?我们 又该如何与它相处？ AI娱乐：当生成变得容易，「值得」由什么决定？产能爆发之后，什么内容值得被看见、值得付费，新的娱乐形式能否成立？ Al落地：模型不会自己走进现场。从「调用多少Token」到「创造多大价值」真正做出结果的企业 和个体，跨过了哪些障碍？ Maker与新匠人：当3D打印、CNC等工具走进个人工作台想法变成实物的路径正在变短。一个人 的兴趣，能有多大的想象空间？

title: 客户为什么愿意为端侧 AI 买单？五位一线操盘手讲透了
summary: 过去几年，AI 行业热衷于比参数、拼算力、讲融资。但模型一旦离开展台，客户的问题立刻具体起来：数据会不会泄露？设备能不能 24 小时运行？响应够不够快？噪声大不大？ 这些问题，正把端侧 AI 推到产业舞台中央。 10 月 14 日，后摩智能在北京开了一场生态合作伙伴大会。期间，极客公园创始人 & CEO 张鹏主持了一场圆桌，五位来自不同赛道的人坐到了一起：麒麟软件副总经理 / 生态发展中心总经理姚翎、聊趣智能科技创始人兼 CEO 黄隽实、罗格数据 CTO 刘学鹏、寅谱计算 CMO 陈展凌、后摩智能 AI 系统总工程师陈仲铭。 他们分别来自操作系统、应用、数据工程、整机集成和芯片领域，讨论的是同一件事：端侧 AI 什么时候才能真正成为一门生意？ 黄隽实讲了一个养老院里的故事。他们在上海落地了一套「数字家人」，陪老人聊天、提醒用药、辅助防诈骗。老人每天说了什么、身体状况如何，都是极其敏感的信息，不能随意上传云端；系统又要全天值守，设备还不能嗡嗡作响。到了这样的现场，隐私、算力、功耗和噪声都不再是技术指标，而是老人愿不愿意使用的前提。 在企业市场，答案同样清晰。刘学鹏认为，客户最关心的是私域化专属。「AI 未来会成为企业的数字专家或数字员工，这种触及核心业务的『员工』，必须招进公司内部，而不是变成外部的云端服务。」当模型开始读取发票、财报、订单和客户资料，数据边界就不再是附加选项，而是商业落地的前提。 对央企及关键岗位而言，安全门槛更加严格。姚翎表示，只要 AI 工具部署在互联网上，涉密数据就绝对不能碰。大模型甚至可能从不同时段上传的碎片信息中，拼凑出完整内容。「本地安全是重中之重，没有任何商量的余地，安全就是一切的前提。」 不过，需求成立，不等于生意成立。 陈展凌直言，客户未必在意省了多少 Token，他们更关心体验。首字出来要多久，机器是否安静，系统会不会卡顿，能否连续稳定运行，这些看似琐碎的问题，决定了产品是被长期使用，还是演示结束后被塞进柜子。 端侧 AI 的难点，不只是把大模型装进小设备，更是把通用能力变成可持续交付的专业服务。模型发布后能否及时适配，硬件成本能否降到客户可接受的范围，软件伙伴能否低门槛开发，都会影响商业化的速度。 而在底层，端侧算力还要面对算力、带宽与功耗的「不可能三角」。陈仲铭说，后摩要做的，就是不断把这三条边界向外推，并通过开放软件、接口和 API，让更多开发者参与进来。 在对话的最后，刘学鹏给了一个大胆的判断：在中国，AI 真正落地，一定是「端侧为主，云端为辅」。端侧是个人和企业的专属大脑，云端是负责知识流动的社会大脑。 这个判断对不对，日后会见分晓。但有一点已经很确定：AI 从「能聊天」走向「能干活」，就要吃进你最核心、最不愿示人的数据。到那时，算力放在哪里，就不再只是技术选型题，而是一道信任题。 大模型的上半场，人们争相让机器变聪明。下半场，比拼的是如何让智能走出云端，进入千行百业。最后的赢家，未必拥有最大的模型，但一定最早跨过那「最后一百米」。 以下是张鹏和姚翎、黄隽实、刘学鹏、陈展凌、陈仲铭的对话内容，部分有删减。 01 安全、私域、体验：端侧 AI 商业化的三道真实门槛 张鹏：去年大家都在说端侧 AI 元年，今年变成了「商业化元年」。在真实的落地过程中，客户掏钱时最在意的是什么？ 黄隽实： 落地过程中的挑战其实非常多。我们在上海一家养老机构落地了「数字家人」场景，主要为了缓解老年人因孤独引发的各类并发症。 在这个场景里，我们特别关注几个核心诉求：首先是安全隐私。家庭场景的私密信息极度敏感，特别是与公办或民营机构合作时，本地算力提供了最好的数据兜底方案。 其次是决策能力。系统需要 24 小时值守，提醒老人用药甚至防诈骗，这要求本地 AI 必须具备强大的持续计算能力。 最后是要非常安静。我们在使用后摩芯片时，能够达到这样一个需求。 刘学鹏： 围绕企业和专业客户来看，大家最关心的是「私域化专属」。 这跟企业的核心利益直接挂钩。企业的核心业务和数据必须掌握在自己手里。AI 未来会成为企业的数字专家或数字员工，这种触及核心业务的「员工」必须招进公司内部，而不是变成外部的云端服务。端侧对企业最大的价值，就是帮他们构建专属的数据与经验边界。 我们今年落地了很多央企和上市公司客户。比如财税场景，大量的发票、财报和订单数据，天然不可能放到云端模型去推理，必须专属化。 现在企业很难规划庞大的算力中心，也不知道算力到底该怎么用。我们现在的模式是，企业哪个岗位缺能力，我们就派一个「数字专家团」进去。这种形态对算力要求没那么大，后摩这样的端侧算力完全能满足。这是一种效果驱动的投资，从小切口切入，是目前端侧非常关键的驱动力。 对于个人部分，我们现在做「专家」体系，比如咨询顾问、税务师等。他们同样在意个人经验和客户资料的隐私。如果用云端 AI，脱敏资料的过程会让人非常痛苦，严重拖累工作效率。 我们今年还做了一些让端侧设备与机器人本地直联的场景。 现在很多机器人的行动能力不错，但知识推理能力不够。我们用端侧设备跟机器人实时打通，直接解决了推理和时延的问题。特别是在工业场景下，这种低时延的端侧优势是不可替代的。 张鹏：除了隐私、私域化部署，端侧真正的核心推动力还有哪些？ 姚翎： 麒麟软件的客户多是党政、央企等核心领域的关键岗位。今年，大家都在规划把 AI 作为重要抓手，政策也全面导向 AI，但现实是客户「不敢用」。 为什么？因为只要 AI 工具部署在互联网上，涉密数据就绝对不能碰。现在 AI 太聪明了，你以为给文件换个代号就安全了？它完全能把今天和明天上传的碎片信息，拼凑出一份完整的涉密文件。 所以对重要岗位的客户来说，本地安全是重中之重。没有任何商量的余地，安全就是一切的前提。 陈展凌： 就我个人感受而言，省 Token 不是客户最主要的痛点，客户体验才是。 就像黄总提到的，端侧设备放在现场一定要静音，我们甚至会考虑加入液冷机制。大家知道首字生成时间会直接影响感受。客户第一次用可能觉得惊艳，但要让他们持续用下去，就必须在端侧把体验做到极致。这不仅仅是芯片和模型的事，整个系统架构的集成与优化同样关键。 陈仲铭： 大家总提「元年」，是因为感觉到风来了。但风向总在变，客户的需求也千差万别。有的要大算力，有的要大带宽做实时交互，还有的需要多模态感知。 这里存在一个「不可能三角」：算力、带宽和功耗。后摩目前做得最好的是解决了功耗问题，接下来的目标就是打破这个不可能三角。 我们规划了两条线。一条是把算力做大，也就是我们的 M 系列。另一条是通过更先进的工艺和封装技术，把带宽做大。这就是我们正在做的事，尽可能去满足千行百业不同的场景需求。 02 下一步，在于生态、成本与规模化 张鹏：底层芯片的地基打牢，端侧的优势才能真正发挥。未来一年，各位对端侧 AI 最期待的发展目标是什么？ 陈展凌： 虽然说是商业化元年，但目前端侧 AI 还远未普及。真实的落地场景依然不够丰富，规模化扩展的步伐还有些慢。我非常期待能有更多的软件商看到这个机遇，果断向端侧 AI 转型。 刘学鹏： 从我们的角度，核心诉求就一句话，Day 0 适配。国内基础算力和模型之间的核心壁垒其实就是生态。我们非常希望后摩能做到所有模型的 Day 0 适配。 黄隽实： 我的要求比较苛刻，希望端侧的「不可能三角」能再往前推一推。实际落地中，成本是极其关键的因素。除了少数预算充足的机构，绝大多数企业并没有巨额的专项资金。这种情况下，极致的成本控制直接决定了商业化的成败。 姚翎： 我的期许很直接，希望今天展示的那些达到量产标准的整机，能快速落地。我希望在后摩下一代 A20 和 M60 芯片出来前，真正实现规模化应用。 技术不用，就永远不知道差距在哪。千万别像我减肥一样，天天马不停蹄地收藏视频，却从来不练。 国产芯片能发展到现在，得益于国家把最大的应用场景开放了出来。如果没有真刀真枪的实战，我们永远会被卡脖子。期待一年后这些设备都能大卖，也请后摩务必把货备足。 陈仲铭： 刚才几位嘉宾提了不同的期许，包括供应链、模型适配、安全保障以及打破不可能三角。对后摩来说，未来的目标其实很纯粹。我们会把硬件做扎实，把软件做好用，全力支撑好各位的商业化服务。 03 从算力到交付，差的不只是技术 张鹏：哪怕芯片和场景都准备好了，要真正变成一台有效运行的设备，工程上还需要下哪些苦功夫？ 陈展凌： 芯片、模型和操作系统只是必要条件。从工程实践来看，主板、散热、机柜设计，以及针对客户体验的优化参考设计，都需要跟现有模型能力做深度适配。国内最大的优势在产业链，我们可以把这些优势转化成端侧可交付的产品，再跟生态伙伴配合，完成端到端的最终交付。 刘学鹏： 我们更关注面向用户的「最后一百米」。模型解决了一公里外的问题，算力解决了五百米的问题，但客户只愿意为最后一百米买单。这是非常关键的商业判断标准。 从应用落地来看，我们面临几道核心门槛。首先是数据打通。模型进企业就像咨询顾问进场，没有业务数据什么活都干不了，原有系统的整合与数据质量必须解决。其次是交互方式。企业用户很难接受纯对话式的逻辑，必须把 AI 无缝嵌入到他们最熟悉的工作流里。最难的一点是稳定性。模型本质上是概率学，但比如做财务报表合并，需要极度精准的匹配计算，这就需要大量的工程技巧来兜底。 谈到付费意愿，现在必须切中用户的绝对痛点。AI 时代最好的产品经理其实在用户现场，他们最清楚自己需要什么样的助理。过去做软件是交付一套系统，现在落地 AI，更像是把一个无所不能的天才，调教成勤勤恳恳、安全可信的专属专家。模型像千里马，我们的工程价值就是帮用户「驯马」。而且面对海量的个性化需求，仅靠堆人力去实施已经不划算了，必须用 AI 去交付 AI，这是现阶段在最后一百米还能赚到钱的唯一出路。 黄隽实： AI 能发展到今天，本身就是工程化不断完善的过程。从早期的提示词工程，到现在的自定义智能体，工程化是让 AI 真正变得可用、好用、用得起的关键。 在我们交付给客户的价值里，工程和服务各占一半。国内开源生态特别好，但在海量开源组件里选出最适合客户的方案，需要跟大量垂直行业用户深度交流。把这些摸索沉淀成可迭代的工程化方法，是非常核心的能力。 姚翎： 端侧要想真正破局，最大的工程其实是「生态工程」。核心在于开放与聚合。大家专注做自己的事，芯片公司做算力，操作系统赋能硬件，应用厂商做交付。我们需要把碎片化的算力架构和各种模型提前做好适配，把生态前置，比如构建端侧的 AI 基础设施。这能帮我们提前验证用户需求，也是未来两年 AI 发展的重头戏。 张鹏：既然提到生态，从后摩的角度，你们希望建设一个怎样的生态？ 陈仲铭： 生态的链条非常长，AI 迭代又太快，我们不可能把所有东西都自己做。所以我们选择把软件开源，把接口、架构和 API 全面开放出去。我们要让开发者和软件商能直接把后摩的产品当成趁手的工具，而不是手把手去教。我们必须把底层基建修好，上面才能跑越来越多种类的车，这就是我们扎根做生态的根本原因。 04 端侧 AI 的未来生态 张鹏：在云端大模型领域，产业结构很清晰：英伟达在最前面提供算力，往后是模型大厂，再往后是做数据、做工程交付的，最后是各类应用。未来端侧 AI 的商业逻辑也是这样吗？ 陈展凌： 无论云端还是端侧，客户最终都是为结果买单。他们买的是一项服务，或者一个数字助理。因此，价值链的顶端一定是 AI 智能体的应用层。我们这些做端侧配套生态的伙伴，核心任务就是支撑这些应用真正在端侧跑起来。 陈仲铭： 在推理时代，市场不可能一家独大，必然是百花齐放的格局。在这个百花齐放的生态里，我希望后摩是开得最漂亮的那朵花。 姚翎： 我最早接触「存算一体」概念就是后摩普及的。从第一款 M30 我们就开始合作，到现在 M50 真正投入量产，甚至能在本地跑通 35B 的大模型，这说明端侧 AI 已经初步具备了让用户掏钱的商业价值。 所以我特别呼吁，今年一定要真正走向客户端。客户到底买不买单，完全取决于 AI 能带来多少实际价值。我相信随着下一代带宽更大、体验更好的芯片推出，只要生态伙伴一起努力，从客户端获取正向反馈，后摩完全有机会成为中国端侧算力的重要力量。 刘学鹏： 中国独特的开源生态，其实是端侧 AI 最天然的土壤。模型一旦开源，形态和规格丰富了，匹配的硬件需求自然会爆发。 谈到场景，大家现在对端侧的想象还局限在 PC 或服务器上。但我认为，AI 时代的端侧设备形态会彻底超出我们的想象。比如今年很火的 AI 录音卡，技术人员一开始可能不看好，但市场就是买单。未来的趋势，应该是把物联网用 AI 的逻辑重做一遍。 关于终局，我个人的判断是，在中国环境下，AI 真正的落地一定是「端侧为主，云端为辅」。

title: OpenAI 三个神秘模型曝光；DeepSeek 开放搜索与网页抓取 API；智界将获独立造车资格，公司计划上市 ｜ 极客早知道
summary: OpenAI 三个神秘模型曝光 10 月 18 日，有开发者发现，OpenAI 的 API 模型列表中突然出现了三个陌生名字： aurora-red-alpha、aurora-green-alpha、aurora-blue-alpha。三个模型都以 Aurora（极光）命名，分别对应红、绿、蓝三种颜色。但相关条目很快便从模型列表中消失。 此次发现来自第三方维护的 OpenAI 模型列表镜像，并非官方公告。因此，这些模型究竟是什么、是否会正式发布，目前都还是未知数。 有网友推测，这些模型极有可能是 GPT-6 Astra 后续版本的内部检查点，专门对标 Fable 5.5 的强项，创意编码、长程 agent、视觉 / 3D。也有网友推测：三个模型对应 OpenAI 三个图像模型。（消息来源：机器之心） Anthropic 与法律专家讨论 AI Agent 谈判规则，未来可替用户砍价、处理纠纷 据《金融时报》最新报道，Anthropic 正在与律师事务所及法律专家合作，研究 AI Agent 代表用户进行谈判时应遵循的行为规范。 随着 Agent 逐渐能够独立执行任务，未来可能出现大量 AI 与 AI 之间的商业交互。 例如，消费者让自己的 AI 助手与商家的 AI Agent 讨价还价，员工让 AI 代理参与薪资谈判，或者用户委托 AI 处理服务纠纷。 Anthropic 希望明确几个问题：AI 应该在多大程度上争取用户利益？什么时候需要征求用户确认？面对其他 AI Agent 时，是否应该默认对方存在欺骗或操纵意图？ 公司还讨论过一种授权方式：让用户通过签署文件，明确 AI 的代理权限、目标和行为边界。 目前，这仍属于规则研究和产品探索，尚未推出面向公众的自动谈判服务。（消息来源：金融时报） DeepSeek 正式开放搜索与网页抓取 API，每千次调用收费 5 元 DeepSeek 正式开放 Search 和 Fetch 两项 API，向开发者提供基于自研搜索引擎的网页搜索及内容抓取能力。 其中，Search API 可以根据关键词返回结构化搜索结果，包括网页标题、链接、摘要、发布日期等信息；Fetch API 则可以抓取指定网页，将正文转换为 Markdown 文本。 两项 API 均采用按成功请求次数计费的方式，价格为每千次 5 元。失败、超时或未返回有效结果的请求不收费。 DeepSeek 还为接入其 API 的 Claude Code、Codex 和 DeepSeek Harness 提供了阶段性的免费搜索调用安排。 DeepSeek 表示，其自研搜索引擎目前每天在全球范围内处理数亿次请求。（消息来源：DeepSeek 官方公告） Anthropic title: The new economics of enterprise AI
summary: Imagine your company just discovered electricity. At first only a few machines run on it, and nobody worries about efficiency — consumption is low and the value is obvious. But once electricity becomes infrastructure, every process depends on it, and the question changes from “can we use it?” to “how efficiently are we using it?” Enterprise AI is going through the same shift. What began as isolated chatbot and copilot experiments is becoming a foundational layer of the business, with models, agents, and data increasingly interconnected in production workloads. The important question stops being what a token or GPU-hour costs. It becomes how efficiently the AI environment converts paid capacity into useful business outcomes. That’s the metric worth tracking: effective cost per useful outcome — the total platform, model, operations, and capacity cost required to complete work the business can actually use, whether a resolved request or a completed workflow. Three ways to run AI Utilization is central to the economics. Directing more work to paid-for capacity lowers effective unit cost; idle GPUs, fragmented workloads, and oversized models all raise the cost of every useful result. title: AI adoption by industry shows what other sectors can learn
summary: The current narrative around artificial intelligence in the workplace is largely driven by Silicon Valley. But treating the tech sector as an island misses the actual trends in technology adoption–tech is just the first industry in line. As generative AI and automation tools mature, the shifts currently reshaping software engineering and product management will inevitably filter into healthcare, education, retail, and manufacturing. The variation in adoption rates today isn’t a sign that non-tech industries are falling behind, but rather a reflection of the different speeds at which industries absorb new workflows. For leaders and their teams outside of tech, this differential pace provides a practical blueprint for how AI adoption unfolds, and where the opportunities lie. The AI adoption spectrum by industry Recent survey data from TripleTen highlights just how stark the current adoption curve is across different sectors of the economy (see Figure 1). title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
summary: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. title: My obituary for programming
summary: My obituary for programming Jeremy Scheff poignantly captures the key loss caused by coding agents for career programmers who enjoyed the puzzle of developing code: Programming turned into one of the greatest jobs you could imagine. You got paid to work on tricky little logic puzzles. The trickier the puzzle, the more you got paid. But even pretty simple puzzles were worth a lot of money because regular people just couldn't do it! No, they needed us. They would give us a problem and we would solve it the way we wanted. We set the strategy, we made the timeline, we defined what was and was not possible. If you're a programmer who thrives on building working systems and doesn't care too deeply about the problems solved along the way, LLMs are the gift that keeps on giving. title: Fintech Funding Fell 21% In Q3 As Deals Grew Scarcer
summary: Venture funding into fintech startups slid 21.4% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, while deal count fell nearly 31%, Crunchbase data shows, pointing to a narrower funding market with fewer rounds and continued reliance on large transactions. All told, fintech startups raised $10.6 billion globally in the third quarter of 2026, down 28.4% from $14.9 billion in Q2 2026 and 21.4% from $13.5 billion in Q3 2025. The pullback comes as investors draw sharper distinctions between companies attracting capital and those struggling to raise, according to QED Investors partner Laura Bock . “The market remains bifurcated — AI vs. not and market leaders vs. not,” she said. Forerunner founder Kirsten Green similarly described capital concentrating in fewer, larger rounds, with infrastructure, payments and stablecoin rails attracting investor interest, supported by greater regulatory clarity. Deal count drops Notably, deal count in Q3 was the lowest in the quarters covered by our analysis, dating back to the first quarter of 2018. Just 687 fintech funding rounds were recorded globally in the third quarter, compared with 789 in the previous quarter and 995 in the same period a year earlier. title: LatAm Startup Funding Jumps 26% In Q3 As VCs Begin ‘Rediscovering’ The Region
summary: A continued boom in late-stage and growth funding combined with a surge in seed-stage funding helped buoy venture investment in Latin America for the third quarter of 2026, Crunchbase data shows. All told, startups in Latin America raised a combined $1.3 billion across seed- and growth-stage deals in the three-month period ending Sept. 30. That was up 26% year over year but down 9% from the second quarter. For perspective, we charted out total investment, color-coded by stage, for the past 12 quarters below. Of the quarterly total, $757 million went into late-stage and growth deals, up 74% compared to the $435 million that flowed into such deals in the third quarter of 2025. However, that is down 21.3% from the $962 million in late-stage and growth rounds raised by LatAm startups in the second quarter. (Although it’s worth noting that Q2 2026 represented the most raised at that stage since the second quarter of 2022.) Mexico startups have raised $1.52 billion in venture funding during the first three quarters of 2026, per Crunchbase data. title: The FDE Bubble: Silicon Valley’s Most Expensive Game Of Pretend
summary: By Anurag Gurtu Congratulations to the enterprise AI company that just raised another nine-figure round to solve a problem software is supposed to solve by itself: getting humans to use the product. You know the one. Won’t name it. Don’t have to. You’ve read the press release — “autonomous,” “agentic,” “category-defining” in paragraph one, and then, a few paragraphs down, where the money is actually going: hiring an army of engineers to sit inside customer offices and manually make the “autonomous” thing behave. Nothing says “we’ve built the future of work” quite like raising half a billion dollars to hire more people to do the work. The business model, decoded Anurag Gurtu, co-founder and CEO of Airrived. Here’s how it works, in case the deck was too artfully vague: Sell the customer an “AI platform.” Discover the platform doesn’t actually do the thing on its own. Send in the forward deployed engineers: sharp young people with CS degrees who now spend six months hand-building the workflow the website implied already existed. Daytona hits $1B valuation with $60M Series B for AI agent cloud
summary: Daytona , a company developing cloud infrastructure for AI agents, has raised $60 million in a Series B funding round at a $1 billion valuation, bringing its total funding to $91 million. The round was led by FirstMark , with participation from Patrick Collison (Stripe), Adam D’Angelo (Quora), Brendan Foody (Mercor), Tobi Lütke (Shopify), Olivier Pomel (Datadog), Aravind Srinivas (Perplexity) and Eric Yuan (Zoom). Other investors included Alumni Ventures, Evergreen Fund, Okta Ventures, Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Next and Torch Capital. Existing investors also increased their commitments, with Pace Capital doubling its investment, Upfront Ventures tripling and E2VC quadrupling theirs. Daytona develops cloud infrastructure that provides secure, isolated computing environments where AI agents can execute code, use software tools and perform tasks. Its platform enables AI developers and enterprises to train and evaluate models, as well as deploy and manage AI agents in production. As AI systems increasingly move beyond answering questions to performing tasks autonomously, companies face growing infrastructure demands. Running large numbers of agents simultaneously requires computing resources that can scale according to demand while maintaining security and isolation between individual agents. title: EIT launches €40M funding call to help bring university deep tech research to market
summary: The European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT) has launched a new call to strengthen the capacity of higher education institutions to turn their research into innovations focused on the manufacturing and deep tech areas. the EIT Higher Education Initiative aims to help universities develop innovation and entrepreneurship skills, turn research into commercial products, and build stronger links with businesses. Backed by €40 million from the EIT, the 2026 funding round will offer up to €1.25 million per selected project over 18 months. Universities, businesses, research organisations, public bodies, and other partners are invited to apply together. The selected projects will help universities develop practical innovation and entrepreneurship skills among students and staff, particularly in STEM, manufacturing, and deeptech. They will also help universities turn research into commercial products, better manage intellectual property, and share expertise. With support from the EIT’s Knowledge and Innovation Communities (KICs), universities will build stronger connections with businesses, investors, and the wider startup community. Martin Kern, Director of the EIT, said: "Turning a research breakthrough into a successful business takes skills, confidence and targeted support. title: Silent sailing, noisy generators: Hydrogen startups PowerUP and H2Boat tackle yachting's diesel problem
summary: PowerUP Energy Technologies , the Estonian company renowned for its advanced hydrogen fuel cell-based electric generators, today announced a strategic partnership with H2Boat , an Italian marine hydrogen technology startup developing integrated solutions for onboard hydrogen production, storage, and use. Check out our earlier interview with PowerUP CEO Ivar Kruusenberg. The partnership aims to give yacht owners and shipyards a practical pathway to quieter, cleaner onboard energy systems by combining complementary technologies to deliver a complete, integrated zero-emission energy solution. H2Boat, a spin-off from the University of Genoa, brings core expertise in marine hydrogen systems and proprietary metal hydride storage technology. Its solutions are engineered for on-board integration, addressing a key challenge for hydrogen in the maritime sector: storing hydrogen safely and efficiently in a form compatible with the constraints of recreational and professional vessels. The joint solution is designed to eliminate vibrations, noise, and greenhouse gas emissions, returning only pure water to the environment in a perfect circular-economy application. "As a lifelong sailor, I know firsthand the absolute peace of being out on the open water, completely in tune with nature. title: Nvidia invests in four German startups as part of $10BN European investment pledge
summary: Nvidia is investing in four German startups, it said yesterday, as part of a multi-billion-dollar investment across Europe, as the chip company's charm offensive across the continent continues. The US chip giant is investing in AI robotics startup Agile Robots , AI healthtech startup Avelios Medical , AI audio startup Mirelo and space technology startup Reflex Aerospace . Nvidia is an existing investor in German startups n8n and Black Forest Labs. The four new investments, for an undisclosed size, follow recent startup investments Nvidia has announced in France and the UK, as its CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang takes part in a whirlwind tour of Europe, which also included a visit to Sweden. The investments are part of a nearly $10bn investment by Nvidia across European tech, investing in startups, universities, and research institutions, as Nvidia looks to maintain momentum behind AI by investing across the ecoystem. The new investments were announced as Huang visited Germany, speaking to German chancellor Friedrich Merz about Germany’s AI roadmap and the industrial applications of AI. The conversation focused on how Germany can make the most of the AI revolution by playing to its strengths in manufacturing and automotive. Nvidia and Germany also announced

title: Coherence Quantum raises €2.78M to tackle quantum computer scaling challenges
summary: Finnish quantum hardware startup Coherence Quantum has raised €2.78 million in a seed funding round to develop its cryogenic signalling and control technology for quantum computers. The round was led by Lifeline Ventures , with participation from technology entrepreneur Mårten Mickos. Originating from Aalto University’s Quantum Computing and Devices (QCD) research group, Coherence Quantum is developing an integrated cryogenic signalling and control platform designed to address infrastructure challenges associated with scaling quantum processors. As quantum computers become more powerful, increasing the number of qubits also requires more complex control and readout systems. Conventional approaches involve additional wiring and signal-conditioning hardware within environments with limited space and cooling capacity, while quantum processors must remain protected from thermal noise and other disturbances that can affect performance. Coherence Quantum aims to address these challenges by developing technologies that improve signal conditioning and enable more efficient connections between control systems and quantum processing units. Aashish Sah , CEO and co-founder of Coherence Quantum, explained that scaling quantum computers requires not only increasing the number of qubits but also developing the infrastructure needed to support them. title: Blackwall hits $2.2B valuation with $100M Series C just weeks after joining Estonia's unicorn club
summary: Web traffic management platform Blackwall today announced it has raised $100 million in Series C at a valuation of $2.2 billion. Last month it was reported that Blackwall reached a €1 billion valuation and ranked fifth in TopTech 2026, the annual ranking of Estonia's 30 most valuable tech companies. AVP , who join existing investors Dawn Capital , MMC Ventures and Tera Ventures , led the round. The new round of financing accelerates Blackwall's objective to build a global traffic management ecosystem around its hosting-provider network. By connecting providers, infrastructure and technology, Blackwall aims to provide greater control over how internet traffic is managed, secured and monetised. Currently spanning bot mitigation, DDoS protection, web application firewall, load balancing, server-side encryption and management of agentic AI traffic, which is rapidly taking over the Internet, Blackwall is deployed inside the web hosting providers’ own infrastructure, identifying real visitors and legitimate automated traffic from malicious bots, attacks and traffic abuse, filtering billions of requests per day. "The web is becoming more automated, more distributed and more complex, but the infrastructure that powers it remains highly fragmented," said Nikita Rozenberg, Co-Founder and CEO of Blackwall. title: Ganiga secures €2.5M to expand its AI-powered food waste technology
summary: Italian deeptech startup Ganiga has raised €1.5 million in an equity funding round to further develop its AI-powered waste management technology and support commercial expansion. The round was led by Italian contract catering company Vivenda, with participation from London-based NextSTEP and three angel investors. Together with €1 million secured through Smart&Start Italia, an incentive programme managed by Invitalia, Ganiga's total funding has reached €2.5 million. Founded in the province of Pisa by Nicolas Zeoli , Ganiga develops technologies combining artificial intelligence, computer vision and robotics to improve waste management and reduce food waste. The company initially focused on robotic waste sorting, developing devices that identify and separate different types of waste. It has sold more than 300 devices for use in airports, shopping centres and large businesses across Italy, Japan, Australia and other European countries. Building on data collected through these deployments, Ganiga expanded into food waste management with HooolyFood, an AI-powered system designed to help catering operators monitor and reduce waste. Using cameras installed above waste containers, the system identifies discarded food without requiring weighing and provides data to help operators identify inefficiencies, improve purchasing and menu planning, and manage costs. title: Former Google DeepMind top researcher launches London “compute-efficient” AI company
summary: A London-based AI company co-founded by a former Google DeepMind research lead and AlphaGo co-creator is launching today, pursuing a “compute-efficient” alternative path to Anthropic and OpenAI’s frontier AI models in progressing AI. Thore Graepel, who left Google DeepMind this summer, is launching AI company Metis Reasoning , which is understood to be initially raising tens of millions of dollars, marking the latest AI company springing up out of London. Graepel, who is a co-creator of AlphaGo, an AI programme developed by Google DeepMind which made history by defeating human players at the Chinese board game of Go, and his co-founders have put together a 12-strong team. The team is made up of researchers, mathematicians, robotics experts and tech entrepreneurs to pursue a different approach to AI reasoning, the process whereby an AI system works through a problem, connecting information, rather than producing an answer based on learning patterns. The launch of Metis (named after the Greek goddess of wisdom), which believes its thesis will lend itself well to industries such as robotics and engineering, comes as investors pour millions into alternative AI systems to LLMs. Metis’s founding team is Graepel; Piers Ingram, a serial technology and biotech entrepreneur who

title: Danish startup Plinto raises €2.9M to streamline financial controls
summary: Copenhagen-based AI startup Plinto has raised €2.9 million in a funding round from People Ventures and Emblem to further develop its AI-powered financial transaction monitoring platform, expand its enterprise customer base and support its first steps into international markets. Founded in early 2025 by Jakob Nielsen , Nermina Suljevic and Sebastian Rehnby , Plinto develops AI agents that help companies identify and resolve errors in financial transactions. The platform automates checks that finance teams typically perform manually, helping ensure that transactions comply with contracts, budgets and internal policies. Plinto integrates with companies' existing systems, including enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, documents, banking systems and communication tools such as Slack and Microsoft Teams. Its AI agents check transactions against agreed terms, investigate discrepancies and collect supporting evidence. When an issue is identified, the agents can follow up with relevant parties, contact suppliers about incorrect invoices, request credit notes or prepare corrections for approval. The company aims to address challenges faced by larger businesses, where high transaction volumes often lead finance teams to rely on spot checks or month-end reviews. title: NOVUS secures eight-figure funding to take its electric Lightbike from Germany to California
summary: Mobility company NOVUS has closed a double-digit million funding round, led by Berlin- and San Francisco-based venture capital firm 468 Capital . The NOVUS One is a lightweight electric two-wheeler that sits somewhere between an e-bike, a scooter, and a motorcycle. Designed for everyday urban travel, it combines the straightforward operation of an electric bicycle with the speed and performance of a motorcycle, without a clutch or conventional gears. Founded in 2019, the Braunschweig-based company began delivering its first vehicle to European customers in spring 2026. I spoke with co-founders René Renger, CEO, and Hannes A. H. Krieger, Chief Strategy Officer, to find out more. From a university design project to a mobility startup NOVUS was founded by Renger, a former Volkswagen designer who worked on the Golf 8 and ID. title: German VCs call for €15B annual funding boost to build the next generation of tech giants
summary: Today the German federal government is holding its first investor conference: the Invest in Germany Summit The event focuses on what Germany needs right now as a business and investment destination. Venture capital leaders warn that the country's reliance on foreign funding risks losing both economic value and control over critical technologies. The German Venture and Growth Forum (GVGF), representing more than 20 leading German venture capital and growth funds with €28 billion in assets under management, argues that Germany must mobilise more domestic institutional capital to finance the next generation of global technology companies. According to figures provided by the Forum, €5.1 billion was invested in German startups during the first half of 2026, but less than a third came from domestic investors. The Forum estimates that Germany could mobilise approximately €15 billion in additional private capital annually for growth companies by increasing institutional allocations to venture capital. Germany's domestic investment gap Germany's startup ecosystem remains heavily dependent on foreign capital, particularly as companies progress into larger funding rounds. According to the GVGF, US investors have provided as much capital as European investors to European companies raising more than €100 million in growth financing over the past five years.

title: Linkener secures €7.5M to expand its energy management platform
summary: Energy technology startup Linkener has raised €7.5 million in a funding round led by Klima Energy Transition Fund, Alantra’s energy transition fund, with existing shareholder GoHub Ventures remaining on board. Linkener has developed an Intelligent Energy Management System (SIGE) that uses proprietary remote metering technology to help businesses and organisations monitor, analyse and optimise their energy consumption. The platform allows customers to track consumption using their own data, digitise and validate energy bills, analyse supply contracts and receive alerts and recommendations to identify potential savings and better manage energy costs. Alongside its technology platform, Linkener supports businesses in implementing energy-saving projects, having completed more than 400 solar and battery storage installations across Spain. The company serves over 2,000 customers and manages 10,000 energy supply points, covering 1.7 TWh of annual energy consumption. The company sees significant opportunities for digitalisation and energy optimisation, particularly in the services sector, where monitoring and controlling consumption can generate savings of 20 per cent. Rising and volatile energy prices, alongside increasingly complex contracts and regulations, are also driving demand for tools that give businesses greater visibility and control over their energy costs. title: Barcelona-based Enzo Ventures closes €20M Fund II backing Southern European founders
summary: Barcelona-based Enzo Ventures has closed its second fund, a €20m fund which is backing Southern European founders at the pre-seed stage. Fund II follows Enzo’s strategy it began in 2023, when it invested in its first fund, which backed Southern European founders and diaspora entrepreneurs at the very start of their journey. Enzo says Fund II has been designed around a simple principle: keep doing what worked in Fund I, a €10m fund, but with more capital and a stronger platform behind it. Enzo defines diaspora entrepreneurs as those founders leaving cities like Barcelona and Lisbon to build companies in cities like London and Paris, while maintaining deep ties to the talent networks and entrepreneurial communities they came from. The firm is looking to identify these founders before the broader VC market. The new fund is deploying cheques of between €250,000 and €600,000. The new fund has already invested in three startups: London-based Cori Clinical and investments in startups in Madrid and Zurich. Enzo’s portfolio includes Orbio and Murphy , which Enzo says are now generating millions of euros in revenue. title: TechWolf co-founder: Ghent flywheel "super important”
summary: One of the co-founders of a Ghent-based AI startup which is being acquired by sofware giant SAP in a deal valued at hundreds of millions of dolllars has stressed the importance of the city’s flywheel effect. Jeroen Van Hautte, CTO and co-founder, TechWolf , was speaking on the Tech.eu podcast, discussing TechWolf's sale to SAP and a range of other issues. The interview follows news earlier this month that German software giant SAP is acquiring TechWolf, in a deal reported to be the largest acquisition of a venture-backed software company in Belgian history. SAP is buying TechWolf, which uses AI to help companies understand their employees' skills and work, saying it would become a key part of its talent and workforce strategy. The CTO discussed the Ghent flywheel impact. A flywheel effect is a cycle, where key employees from startups develop ideas of their own and launch their own startups or fund other startups. title: Vessla exits stealth with $3.3M to bring AI agents to property management
summary: Stockholm-based AI startup Vessla has emerged from stealth with a $3.3 million pre-seed funding round led by Seedcamp . Other participants included Inception Fund, Tiny VC, operators from Lovable and OpenAI, founders Lukas Saari (Tandem Health) and Fredrik Hjelm (Voi, Pit), and several angel investors. The round was more than twice oversubscribed. Founded earlier this year, Vessla is building an AI-powered platform designed to automate workflows across the systems used by residential and commercial property owners and managers. The company is already working with some of the Nordics' largest property owners and operators. Property operations involve coordination between tenants, managers, suppliers and finance teams, often requiring information to be transferred manually between different systems. Tasks such as maintenance requests can involve multiple processes, from reviewing property records and contracts to managing invoices and communicating with suppliers. Vessla aims to simplify these processes by providing a shared AI layer that connects existing business systems. Its AI agents can retrieve relevant information, apply an organisation's operating rules and execute workflows across connected software. Check out these stories: My name is Dave Rouse, founder of CarbonClick. CarbonClick’s mission is to help humans restore the planet and our vision is to be the offset platform of choice to the world’s leading businesses. CarbonClick makes climate action simple, cost-effective, meaningful, and transparent. I am a kiwi born entrepreneur who strives to bring a unique set of sustainability and Tikanga Maori values, into a variety of businesses. I’ve owned over a dozen businesses and co-founded a charity, as well as voluntary mentoring and holding board seats. I set high standards and a great culture of stretch goals, leadership, and support to reach them within our CarbonClick team. Every business or charity is entered into with purpose, vision, and quadruple bottom-line results in mind. CarbonClick is my current focus and is on the right track to becoming another success story for NZ, both at a financial scale as well as a global impact level. I started looking at CarbonClick as an Angel investor to the two other founders, before its formation, but they asked me to lead the business as well as invest. The offering was sound for Airlines and Airports were the next targets once the technology was built. With presales ahead of schedule, they were on a very strong path before the Covid hitting. Together, we’re accelerating meaningful impact with 800 businesses and 99,600 individuals. We ve offset 27+ million kg of carbon emissions. What s your backstory and how did you come up with the idea? My Co-Founders built and monitored the carbon offsetting module for an international airline and discovered four things: People were concerned about their travel footprint and wanted to do something about it. People didn’t have much trust that their dollar wasn’t being taxed by the airline as a revenue-generating activity, because there was no transparency. If we could increase the quality of offsets as well as uptake rates of offsetting globally by airlines, we could really help to restore our planet long term. There was no “off the shelf” solution. It cost half a million to custom build the offsetting software, took a long time, and cost about $150k per annum to continue running the program and software updates. The idea was formed to build a better platform that included full transparency traceability of each offset, and in turn, provide better ability to highlight the more expensive but much higher impact projects we need to be funding. The fact that airlines could save money at the same time by making it a plug-in to their e-commerce solutions was compelling. The founders of CarbonClick got together as we all had a shared purpose and passion for sustainability and bettering our planet. We all knew of each other through the Aviation sector and this led us to come together to offer a solution that is more accessible, trustworthy, meaningful, and most of all, simple. Take us through the process of designing, prototyping, and manufacturing your first product. We were lucky in that we had built a crap solution in the airline, which matched other crap solutions in the market. We were able to gain market validation insights from the customer questions, comments, and these matched the focus groups we ran market validations with. Our co-founders applied for an accelerator to explore how to take this idea into a potential business, and this is where the re-design and prototyping began. We are continuously redefining our product. Describe the process of launching the business. We started with an accelerator program to polish and validate our idea, make up a prototype, and then seek pre-seed funding to further develop our idea into a working platform that could be utilized in the market and expanded further. We then ran a seed round to commercialize and further refine our platform. Seek experience sharing rather than advice, as everyone’s situation will be a little different. We tested different paths to market but our starting point was a direct reach out for months, to find our early adopters who we could leverage. We then launched an official PR campaign in NZ. We used the campaign to drive people to our website and phones. We referenced our first adopters including Mighty Ape, AA SmartFuels, Placemakers, and 10 Shopify stores. We marketed a “spray and pray” model first to sense and check different market opportunities, then tested sales and marketing strategies that worked in these key areas. Where we found a strong interest plus a marketing or sales strategy that worked, we doubled down. We had to say “no for now” to those where we hadn’t found either demand or an economic path to market. Since launch, what has worked to attract and retain customers? The vast majority of our customers are resource/time-constrained but are passionate about taking climate action. One of our core pillars, to make climate action simple, helps address this need. Social media and marketing activities have helped to drive people to know more about our brand. Utilizing Instagram, LinkedIn and Facebook, and EDM’s and PR opportunities. We found that on our social channels, when we include a essence of authenticity by adding our team experiences or creating a shared purpose with our audience that was easily relatable enabled us to connect more with our audience to build and add another layer of transparency and trust with our clients on social media because we don’t want to filter anything - we want everyone to truly see who CarbonClick is and what our mission is. Having this mentality really helps us to stand out from the rest. We also found that doing now and then doing giveaways and boosting posts (ie. partnership announcements) will get a better outcome with thousands of people being reached on socials which then adds more brand recognition and could potentially lead to a prospect client stumbling across our posts. We mainly use Instagram to attract a wider audience - be it SMEs, larger enterprises, or just individuals who are passionate about sustainability. Instagram enables us to communicate with them on the climate crisis and to educate them on ways they can make a positive impact on the planet. LinkedIn on the other hand, we definitely use more professionally and target the bigger enterprises and we use sales navigator on LinkedIn to reach out to our target clients and LinkedIn campaign manager to run ads with educational content or partnership announcements which will then have a CTA to our website or an email address they can contact from our team. If you're interested in reading how they got started, published over 6 years ago, check it out here. Hello again! Remind us who you are and what business you started. I’m Qin Xie , a journalist and editor based in London. In May 2020 I launched Money Talk , a smart newsletter that’s designed to help you save money and grow wealth. Although I managed to secure paying subscribers straight away, I quickly realized that in the UK, a paid newsletter in the personal finance space isn’t going to work so I had to rethink my strategy. In December 2020, Money Talk became a website and newsletter. Less than a year after launch, it was shortlisted for Headlinemoney.co.uk’s Blog of the Year . Tell us about what you’ve been up to! Has the business been growing? Money Talk is very much a side hustle for me at the moment. That means I’m only spending one day a week on it - usually, a Saturday - and I’m not pressured into putting in all my spare time. Because of that though, its growth has varied over the last 15 months. When I launched the project in 2020, I was on furlough so I had a lot more time - time to work on the content and time to promote it on social media and beyond - and I was seeing steady growth in the number of paying subscribers. Even when I first returned to work after furlough, I still had a fair bit of spare time because things weren’t fully open in the UK yet so there weren’t as many distractions in life. That said, things were certainly shifting. In the months that the lockdown restriction eased in 2020, open rates for the newsletter were lower and people might take days before opening the latest edition. It was a sign that I had to make some changes to make this newsletter work. Plus, conscious of the dwindling availability of my own spare time, the newsletter also had to evolve in a way to suit me. That’s why I moved to the website-first model where only premium subscribers get the full content (plus some extra frills) in their inbox - everyone else had to click through to the website. It meant that I could use the newsletter to continue to build my readership but also gain advertising revenue that’s hard to achieve until you have a much higher subscriber base. Plus, the newsletter now has a great clickthrough rate. In January 2021, I went freelance full-time after finishing my contract. I had wanted to use the opportunity to grow Money Talk more, and spend two days a week on it while working four days to pay bills and expenses. As it turned out, my services as a freelancer were in high demand and I’ve been working five-plus days a week, meaning Money Talk remains a one-day-a-week project. At this point, I was working flat out, sometimes seven days a week for weeks at a time. I needed to change the approach to content so it was less labor-intensive - that meant fewer stories per newsletter but each with greater depth. This, I think, is more useful to the reader but perhaps less valuable to premium subscribers, which is why I also decided to lower the subscription fee. Fortunately, since tweaking the content to suit me better, it’s been much easier to find great content every week and the number of subscribers is growing much faster than before. What have been your biggest lessons learned in the last year? Getting honest feedback from my subscribers has been essential to the growth of Money Talk - and that’s something I took away from Y Combinator’s Startup School . In asking them about what they found valuable in Money Talk, I was able to tweak it in a way that worked for me and them. It’s important to look for opportunities to talk about your business but never be pushy. And it certainly shouldn’t be at the expense of having a good product. The other thing is that the media landscape in the UK is very different from the US, where many of the successful newsletter authors are based. In the US, readers are more ready and willing to pay for news and there’s a bigger potential readership. In the UK, newsletters can be successful - but they are much more likely to be B2B rather than B2C. And certainly, I’d need to spend a lot more than one day a week on it. What’s in the plans for the upcoming year, and the next 5 years? I’m working on a couple of big projects in my freelance life that are taking up most of my free time and that won’t change for the next year. I think this is a good thing - it gives me more time to build up the readership for Money Talk and have a serious bank of great content. Think of it as an incubation period, except I don’t have to worry about funding the startup phase. I’m already seeing steady growth in ad revenue from just Google ads and I’ve run a handful of sponsored newsletters. All of these are on top of the revenue I get from paying subscribers. In the next five years, I think this will grow to the point where I can afford to spend more time on Money Talk without worrying about whether or not I have enough income to cover the bills. Have you read any good books in the last year? I haven’t had much time to read but the podcast I’d recommend is The Squiggly Careers Podcast , which is all about navigating a world where we won’t have the same job, with the same company and in the same industry that people traditionally expect. Instead, we might shift forwards, backward, and sideways to achieve job satisfaction. It asks really interesting questions and gets me to think about how I navigate my working life as well as how I can build Money Talk. Advice for other entrepreneurs who might be struggling to grow their business? Every business is different and while you always read about the businesses that go from zero to success, most startups aren’t like that. And, for many people, it’s a long slog with seemingly little progress, and then suddenly all the good karma you’ve accumulated over time just suddenly helps you to take off. It’s important to look for opportunities to talk about your business but never be pushy. And it certainly shouldn’t be at the expense of having a good product. And of course, just because you’ve launched your product, it doesn’t mean it has to stay the same. You can launch it again and again, tweaking it until you’ve found the right product fit.
